title: Does a neural residual on top of the tuned PID get a quadrotor roll controller below the PID error floor?
lede: does a zero-initialised neural residual on the tuned PID beat the PID on a randomised quadrotor? No at equal evaluations (7.68° against 7.58°, better in 7 of 18 pairs); the airframe ranking is unchanged (Spearman 1.00).
summary: Follow-up to codesign-aero-mlp: the controller is the tuned PID plus a 31-parameter residual network that is exactly zero at the start, so CMA-ES begins at the PID. On six airframes spanning the wide-plant ranking, three seeds each, scored on 64 held-out episodes, PID (96 evaluations) plus residual (480) reaches 7.68° mean, against 7.58° for a PID given all 576 evaluations; the residual is better in 7 of 18 airframe-seed pairs and worse in 11, with most of the gap on one airframe. Against the 96-evaluation PID it started from it is better in 14 of 18 but by 0.04° on average, within seed scatter. The airframe ranking is unchanged (Spearman 1.00). A negative result: the error floor is set by gust, sensor noise and motor lag rather than the control-law class in this roll-only model. Limits: evolution strategies rather than PPO, one small network, roll only, six airframes; plant ranges are assumed round numbers carried over from codesign-aero, not measurements.
